explanation:
## 思路

关键观察：两个物体相撞时交换速度，如果把物体看成没有编号的点，效果和“两个点直接穿过对方继续走”完全一样。所以每个初始位置-速度对都会沿直线一直走到边界离开，只是离开的那个物体编号可能变了。

最后一个物体离开的时刻 = 所有“幽灵点”离开时刻的最大值：

- `v > 0`：向右走，用时 `(tableLength - p) / v`。
- `v < 0`：向左走，用时 `p / |v|`。

取最大值后向上取整。

## 正确性

在任意时刻，桌面上物体所占的位置集合与“互相穿过”模型的位置集合相同（碰撞只交换速度，不改变位置集合）。因此桌面上还剩几个物体、何时变空，两个模型完全一致，最后离开时刻就是各幽灵点离开时刻的最大值。

## 复杂度

时间 `O(n)`，空间 `O(1)`（Python 版存了一个列表，`O(n)`，可改为边扫边取最大）。

## 易错点

- 题面写“四舍五入到最近整数（ceiling）”，以括号里的向上取整为准，用 `math.ceil`。
- 速度为 0 的物体在这个模型里永远不会离开，题面没有说明此情况，这里假设所有速度非零；Python 版遇到 0 会得到无穷大并报错，Java/C++ 版则直接忽略它。
- 用浮点除法时注意精度，整除恰好时 `ceil` 不能多加 1；必要时可用整数 `(d + v - 1) // v` 比较分数大小。
- 题面没有样例，只用自造数据验证：`position=[1,4,7], velocity=[1,-2,3], L=10` 得到 9。
explanationEn:
## Approach

Key observation: when two objects collide and swap velocities, treating the objects as unlabeled points makes it identical to the two points passing straight through each other. So every initial (position, velocity) pair travels in a straight line until it leaves the table; only the label of the object that leaves may differ.

The last exit time is the maximum exit time over these "ghost" points:

- `v > 0`: moving right, takes `(tableLength - p) / v`.
- `v < 0`: moving left, takes `p / |v|`.

Take the maximum and round up.

## Correctness

At every moment, the set of occupied positions is the same in both models (a collision swaps velocities but not positions). So the number of objects still on the table, and when it becomes empty, match exactly, and the last exit time is the maximum over the ghosts.

## Complexity

`O(n)` time, `O(1)` space (the Python version keeps a list, `O(n)`; it could track the max on the fly).

## Pitfalls

- The statement says "rounded to the nearest integer (ceiling)"; follow the ceiling in parentheses and use `math.ceil`.
- An object with velocity 0 never leaves in this model. The statement doesn't cover that case, so all velocities are assumed non-zero; the Python version would raise on infinity, while Java/C++ skip it.
- Watch floating-point precision so that an exact division doesn't get bumped up by `ceil`; integer arithmetic like `(d + v - 1) // v` with fraction comparison avoids this if needed.
- No samples in the statement; checked on hand-made data: `position=[1,4,7], velocity=[1,-2,3], L=10` gives 9.
